examples.derivation: The two directed paths have lengths A–C = 3+5 = 8 days and A–B–D–E = 3+4+2+7 = 16 days. Therefore A–B–D–E is the critical path and the minimum completion time is 16 days. The solution highlights exactly these critical edges.

A–D–F and B–C–D–F each take 14 hours; A–E–F and B–C–E–F each take 16 hours. The latter two paths are both critical. The red edges correctly show their union, and the minimum completion time is 16 hours.

Forward event times at S, P, Q, R and Z are 0, 5, 4, max(5+7,4+3)=12 and 14. Backward times are 0, 5, 9, 12 and 14. Activity D has float 12−3−4=5 days. Increasing D by 2 days leaves completion at 14 days. Increasing C by 1 day increases completion to 15 days. All annotated event-time pairs agree.

The known paths B, C–D and C–E–G take 9, 7 and 12 hours respectively. Hence the stated 19-hour minimum requires A–F to take 19 hours: 5+x=19 gives x=14 hours. The solution diagram correctly supplies F=14 and highlights A–F.
